project.description: Name this project's cases are stored under.

url.description: Where the collector answers. Defaults to the local one started by `intersite collector`.

domain.description: Optional custom domain for the collector, such as intersite.example.com.

readTokenEnv.description: Environment variable holding the read token.

ingestTokenEnv.description: Environment variable holding the ingest token.

dailyCap.description: Most cases stored per project per day; the overflow is dropped.

packs.description: Rule packs to turn on. Every rule in a listed pack is an error unless `rules` says otherwise. Everything is on by default except `runtime`, `actions` and `comments`; a framework pack stays silent in a project that does not use the framework. Run `intersite lint --rules` for the list.

rules.description: Per-rule overrides: an Intersite rule by its id (`no-explicit-any: off`), or a rule oxlint ships by its full name (`import/no-cycle: off`).

custom.description: Project-local rules, in the same form as the package's lint/rules.yml.

baseline.description: Findings that already exist; the count per file and rule may only go down.

extends.description: The project's own oxlint config, used when the file exists.

ownRules.description: Whether findings from the project's own oxlint config are reported and baselined too. Set false when the project already runs oxlint with its own baseline or gate: Intersite then reports only the rules its packs and lint.rules turn on, and a change to the project's own rules never touches intersite-baseline.json.

typeAware.description: Runs oxlint's type-aware rules for promises nobody awaits (typescript/no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, await-thenable). Needs the oxlint-tsgolint package and a tsconfig.json; slower than plain lint.

gates.description: Checks on a change (the diff against `base`), run by `intersite check` and `intersite gate <name>`.

base.description: Git ref the change is compared with.

run.description: Gates `intersite check` runs. `fails-on-base` and `mutation` run the tests and need `testCmd`.

testPaths.description: Globs for test files, relative to the project folder.

testCmd.description: Command that runs the tests; exits non-zero on failure. Keep it fast.

setup.description: Command run in a temporary worktree before `testCmd`. When empty, the checkout's node_modules is linked in.

duplicateLines.description: An added block of this many lines that already exists elsewhere is reported.

mutants.description: Most mutants the mutation gate tries per run.

acknowledged.description: Deliberate exceptions. Each one is visible in review: the gate, what it applies to, and why.

gate.description: Gate name, such as test-integrity or new-deps.

target.description: File path (relative to the project folder) or dependency name the exception covers.

entryPaths.description: Extra globs, relative to the project folder, for files that are loaded by convention and never imported (routes, pages, scripts), so `unused` leaves them alone.

artifacts.description: Extra globs, relative to the project folder, for leftover files `artifacts` should report, on top of the built-in list.

sample.description: Share of sessions recorded in full. Cases that are not ok are always recorded.

maxBodyBytes.description: A larger request body is replaced with a marker.

exclude.description: Path globs never recorded, such as webhooks.

redactKeys.description: Extra JSON keys whose values are always replaced, on top of the built-in list.

idPattern.description: Regular expression for values that are IDs; they are kept so replay can remap them. The default takes `prefix_` IDs whose part after the prefix holds a digit or a capital (or is 16 or more characters) and UUIDs; set this when the project's IDs differ (base64url with `-` or `_`, plain numbers).

keepKeys.description: Extra JSON keys whose short codes and ISO dates are kept, on top of the built-in structural and date words. redactKeys and the built-in sensitive list win.

replay.description: Replay of recorded traffic. `replay: false` turns it off for a project that only lints and gates: `intersite check` runs no replay stage and `intersite init` writes no adapter.

target.description: Base URL the cases are replayed against.

adapter.description: Module that signs in seeded users and resolves IDs.

sample.description: Sessions per run when no --sample is given.

uiTarget.description: Base URL of the web app, for the `ui` mode.

shiftDates.description: Move recorded timestamps in requests forward by the time since capture, so date validation still passes.

browser.description: Browser for the `ui` mode. `chrome` uses Chrome Headless Shell when Playwright has it installed, else Google Chrome; `lightpanda` starts `lightpanda serve` from PATH.

browserUrl.description: Chrome DevTools Protocol URL of a browser already running, for the `ui` mode to connect to instead of starting one (http://host:port or ws://...).

snapshotIgnore.description: JSON pointers left out of --snapshot-base comparisons, for values that change on their own; `*` matches one segment (/updatedAt, /items/*/etag).

contractIgnore.description: Deliberate exceptions to the contract replay mode; each silences the findings it matches and shows up in review.

route.description: Method and route template (GET /v1/orders/:id), or the template alone for every method.

pointer.description: JSON pointer of the finding (/data/created_at); omit to match every pointer.

crossTenantIgnore.description: Routes whose records are public by design (a marketplace listing, a network program): the cross-tenant mode does not send them as another account, so neither its access check nor its list check reports them. Shows up in review.

route.description: Method and route template (GET /v1/programs/:id), or the template alone for every method.

why.description: Why another account may reach this record.

pack.description: Pack the rule belongs to. Custom rules are always on and need none.

selector.description: ESLint-style syntax-tree selector; every match is reported.

message.description: What is wrong and what to do instead.

files.description: Path globs the rule applies to; all files when omitted.

ignore.description: Path globs the rule never applies to, such as the one file allowed to do what it bans.

bad.description: Code that must be reported. Checked by the test suite.

good.description: Code that must not be reported. Checked by the test suite.

comment.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) tested against the first line of every comment; a match is reported. Use this instead of `selector` for rules about comments.

unless.description: With `comment`: a regular expression that exempts a comment it matches.

ext.description: File extension the `bad` and `good` examples are checked as; `ts` unless set (use `tsx` for JSX).

skip.description: Kinds of file the rule leaves out: tests (tests, fixtures, stories, mocks, seeds) and generated (a generated/ folder, *.gen.* or *.generated.*, or a generated-file header).

needs.description: Regular expression the file's source must match for the rule to run, checked before any tree work. It must match everything the selector can report.
